chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Malik ibn 'Atiyyah from Dawud ibn Farqad said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a mature slave-girl, and she did not menstruate at his place until six months had passed for her, and there was no pregnancy in her. He said: 'If girls like her do menstruate, and it was not due to old age, then this is a defect, and she is returned because of it.'

key_terms.جَارِيَةً مُدْرِكَةً: A mature slave-girl (who has reached puberty age)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a purchased slave-girl does not menstruate within six months?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *khiyar al-'ayb* (option of defect) in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that physiological anomalies constituting a deviation from the norm for one's age group render a sale voidable. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the absence of menstruation is not merely a delay but a specific defect if it contradicts the biological reality of similar individuals, thereby protecting the buyer from hidden liabilities. This ruling underscores the meticulous attention to natural signs (*alamat*) in commercial transactions within the Shia legal tradition.
